batch: Classify three single-bowl articles from journal, publisher and later-scholarship records
policy: Work-scope judgments only. They do not certify complete object extraction, endorse readings, resolve identities or authenticity, or change text and media rights.

entries.basis: The journal's own article record (Studia Orientalia Electronica, https://journal.fi/store/article/view/49806) gives the full title 'An Aramaic Incantation Bowl from Borsippa. Another specimen of Eastern Aramaic "koiné". Appendix: A Cryptographic bowl text or an original fake?'. The article is devoted to one Borsippa bowl; the appendix discusses a further text whose object status was not inspected, so this does not certify that the appendix edits a second in-scope bowl.

Magnes Press's table of contents for Tarbiz 80/2 and James Nathan Ford's Bar-Ilan publication list both give the article as 'An Incantation Bowl for Rav Mešaršia son of Qaqay', Tarbiz 80 (2011/12): 219-230 [Hebrew]: a twelve-page article devoted to one bowl for one named client. JSTOR metadata for 23607828 describes the same.

Later scholarship on the same bowl, 'Yet Again on the Unique Incantation Bowl BM 135563' (author-deposited, https://www.academia.edu/8295036), names Müller-Kessler and Kwasman, JAOS 120 (2000): 159-165, as the first publication of BM 135563, with Segal 2000 and Morgenstern 2004/2005 as later editions. The article is devoted to that one bowl.
